title: Cost + latency tradeoff hypothesis notes
content:
Purpose
Quick, messy playbook to map specific claim-types to the smallest possible proofs we can run and show to customers (bench + field). Goal: let sales/solutions ship short, defensible lines: not a full whitepaper, but enough to win customers who care about cost/latency tradeoffs.

Context / thesis
- Customers often have to pick between two hard constraints: latency SLOs (p50/p95) and unit cost ($/1M tokens, or $/session).
- Redwood’s differentiators are (a) runtime-level batching + KV prefix caching, (b) smart routing + fallbacks across model variants, (c) quantization + kernel tuning. Those combine to reduce per-token cost without linear latency penalty if we configure workloads correctly.
- Sales asks: "Tell me how you are faster AND cheaper than CloudX / API-Provider / self-hosting" — they need crisp, repeatable claims and 2–3 direct proofs.

High-level claim families (short phrases we can use in pitch)
1) Predictable low tail latency at scale (p95 SLAs for session interactions) — proof: p95 vs qps chart from perf lab + canary in Dedicated.
2) Effective token-level cost reduction via automatic prefix cache + batching — proof: before/after per-session token cost on a chat workload.
3) Seamless fallback to cheaper model variants on overload — proof: demo of same prompt routing to quantized variant under burst.
4) Session amortization: long-lived KV caches reduce tokens-per-response for multi-turn flows — proof: average token savings for 8–15 turn convo.

Small proofs we can run quickly (priority order)
A. Short chat workload bench (priority: 1 week)
- Setup: 4k sample user sessions, median length 6 turns, 8–12 tokens per turn output (toy convo). Compare: hosted default model vs same model with prefix caching vs quantized variant.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens billed (per-session), throughput (req/s), cost per 1k sessions.
- Deliverable: 1p slide + 3 graphs (latency distribution, per-session token cost distribution, throughput vs cost).

B. Microburst burst smoothing test (priority: 2 weeks)
- Setup: simulate traffic spikes (10x qps for 20s) and show graceful degradation via fallback/routing to cheaper region/model.
- Metrics: error rate, p95 while spike, cost delta.
- Deliverable: video capture + short script for live demo.

C. Session amortization math quick model (priority: 3 days)
- Produce a simple calculator: effective tokens billed per user = base prompt + (response tokens * turns) - cache_hits*avg_saved_tokens.
- Example: 10-turn flow, avg response 30 tokens, cache hit 40% -> tokens billed delta ~ -120 tokens/session -> map to $ savings. Add a sensitivity table.

Competitor callouts (quick, not exhaustive)
- CloudX-Managed: often better raw peak throughput because of raw infra footprint but lacks automatic KV prefix caching and integrated fallbacks. Their docs show similar per-token pricing but no clear session amortization example.
- LLM-API-Y: strong for simple single-turn generation; their rate limiting + shared noisy neighbors make p95 unpredictable for multi-turn chat at scale. Use customer anecdotes (anonymized) to support.
- Self-host: lowers model licensing costs sometimes, but ops costs and slow kernel optimization for mixed sequence length workloads make it hard to sustain p95 targets without big infra spend.

Sales-ready claim copy (1–2 lines each)
- "Keep conversations snappy at scale: consistent p95 < 300ms for interactive chat while reducing per-session token bills by up to 30% via automatic KV caching and batching."
- "Tune once, save forever — our runtime auto-selects cheaper quantized kernels when accuracy tolerances allow, cutting inference $/token without engineering lift."
- "When your traffic spikes, we keep the lights on — automated fallback routing to compatible model variants keeps error rates low while controlling unit cost."

Proof rigor levels (what buyer expects vs what we can deliver quickly)
- Level 1 (Field-friendly): short bench + one customer quote/demo (acceptable for SMB/mid-market).
- Level 2 (Buyer diligence): lab reproducible benchmarks + canary Dedicated logs + short postmortem on variance drivers (enterprise RFP).
- Level 3 (Technical diligence): full reproducible artifacts, code, dataset, and third-party verification (rare, later stage).

Sample objection responses (sales)
- "Your p95 numbers are lab-only": show a canary Dedicated run + a customer case where we instrumented p95 and matched our lab within 15%.
- "Cheaper but lower quality": show side-by-side outputs for same prompt at default/quantized variant with simple human-eval pass rates; call out fallbacks if quality dips.
- "Can you prove per-session savings?": demo the session amortization calculator and a real recorded session trace annotated with cache hits.

Quick measurement checklist for bench runs
- record exact model version + quant flags + kernel build id
- use real-ish prompts + anonymize PII
- capture token billing logs and runtime token counters (KV hits/misses)
- capture per-request latency histograms (p50/p75/p95/p99)
- store raw traces for one representative run for slides

Demo / playbook ideas for AE enablement
- "Show-and-tell" deck: 4 slides — problem, quick bench chart, one session trace + calculator, call-to-action (trial with seeded credit).
- Live demo script: start baseline model -> enable prefix caching -> show traces and token counter changes -> trigger a controlled burst -> show fallback routing.
- Customer-facing one-pager: headline claim + 2 metrics + 1 short testimonial + link to trial. Keep under 250 words.

Open questions / risks to track
- Bench to field delta magnitude — need 3 customer canaries to feel confident about p95 claims.
- Pricing math sensitivity to tokenization differences across model families.
- Edge cases: very long context (>8k) and multimodal inputs not covered in this quick playbook.

Next actions (who-does-what)
- Marcus: run quick A bench (A-charts) by Fri (Jira 4512).
- Lena: draft the 4-slide AE deck and the one-pager for demo prep.
- Kai: produce the session-amortization calculator and post link in Confluence.
- Avery: stitch results into a short evidence pack for field (2 slides + demo script).

Notes-to-self (rough)
- keep claims conservative: avoid absolute ms numbers without specifying model + region + seq len.
- package artifacts so solutions engineering can replay in customer environment (scripted infra).
- keep legal looped for any public customer quotes.

Appendix: quick example math (handcalc)
- Baseline per-session tokens: prompt 120 + (4 turns * 40 tokens) = 280 tokens.
- With caching that saves 30 tokens/turn on average (prefix hits), billed = 120 + (4 * 10) = 260 tokens -> 20 token savings (~7%).
- If p50 latency without caching = 160ms and with caching = 140ms (same config), then claim: lower cost AND faster in multi-turn flows (note: require p95 proof).

-- end of draft --
